findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 3, Harm 3
Raise: Not done. Case: normal use - a developer runs `forge work` from a Codex coordinator with Fast enabled in a repo that has no `codex_fast` setting. The owner-approved item is: “A new repo and an upgraded repo with no codex_fast setting run Codex without Fast, and Fast runs only when forge.toml sets codex_fast to needed or always”. `src/forge/worker.py:173,298-301` hands native work to the session before `codex.fast_needed` is called, and `src/forge/native.py:151-160` requests no speed. [Codex 0.159.2](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.159.2/codex-rs/core/src/agent/child_config.rs) applies the coordinator’s tier to its child, so that worker runs with Fast despite the new default. The new test forces `claude_session` at `tests/test_codex_runs_without_fast_by_default.py:12` and exercises only the app-server route. This native route and its tier inheritance are evidence not addressed by the ruling to change the shared default.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Gate. Case: normal use - the pull request’s required test check runs the related suite. The fixtures omit `codex_fast` (`tests/test_codex_worker.py:104-110` and `tests/test_codex_resume.py:168-173`), but `tests/test_codex_worker.py:370-381` expects `fast_wanted` to be true and `tests/test_codex_resume.py:270-277` expects both true and a `priority` request. With the new default, `src/forge/codex.py:483-485` returns false and the requests use the default tier, so both assertions fail. The CI picker includes these tests, leaving the required check red until their expectations or settings are updated.
findings.title: Gate: Existing Codex lifecycle tests still expect Fast by default

stop.reason: Harm 3 or higher findings: one more round by the standing rule

why: Codex Fast is on by default: a repo that leaves codex_fast out gets Fast for every fix and every repair round, and the owner wants it off unless a repo opts in
